clue.text: Non-voting parliamentarians monopolise London venue

parts.note: the Speaker of a parliament chairs debates and does not normally vote
to corner a market is to monopolise it

explanation.surface: Some members of parliament who cannot vote take over a London meeting place.
explanation.walkthrough: Speakers' Corner is the spot in London's Hyde Park where anyone may stand up and address the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The open-air free-speech spot in Hyde Park is a famous London place for public oratory.

clue.text: What B&Q's doing to supply plasterer's seasonal extra?

definitions.text: What B&Q's doing to supply plasterer's
definitions.meaning: B&Q is a British DIY chain, which stocks the paste that plasterers use to plug cracks
a small present put in a Christmas sock

explanation.surface: A DIY store keeps plastering supplies for the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Small gifts packed into a Christmas sock are a festive bonus beside the main presents.

clue.text: Comparatively vain agency worker's first to quit bank

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for the agency worker leaves

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker from an agency
a tier is a row or bank, as of seats

explanation.surface: An agency temp is the first to leave the bank, more in vain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vain' is not conceited here but futile, hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain in the sense of hollow or futile; more hollow is a comparative of empty.

clue.text: Restriction on pavement artist's work hampers style, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals the words are spoken, to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: curbs means hampers, and tone means style

explanation.surface: A limit on street art cramps the artist's style.
explanation.walkthrough: Kerb is the British spelling of the American curb, the edge of a pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: The edging stone of a pavement marks the boundary where the chalk artist must stop.

clue.text: Gable's touching part rewritten for Eliot

indicators.note: rewritten means written out again in another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clark Gable's moving role is redrafted for T. S. Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gable' suggests the actor Clark Gable; it is the end wall of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A slate or clay unit of roofing lies against the triangular end wall of a building.

clue.text: Busy butcher has no time for this little charmer

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling activity, so the letters are stirred about
has no means lacks, so the letter for time is removed

explanation.surface: A busy butcher has no time for this sweet child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' takes T from BUTCHER, leaving BUCHER, which 'Busy' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A winged infant angel, or by extension a sweet chubby-faced child, is a little charmer.

clue.text: Assemble riding kit first

indicators.note: first puts the word for kit at the front

parts.note: a rig is a set of kit or equipment
up means riding, as in a jockey being up on a horse

explanation.surface: Put together your riding gear before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To rig something up is to put it together, often roughly, from parts at hand.

clue.text: Mistake made by a bishop in not speaking up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
in places the a and bishop inside the word for silent

parts.note: mute means not speaking
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop errs by keeping quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ARR inside MUTE to make MUTARRE; 'up' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: An error in a printed book, often listed on a correction slip, is a mistake.

clue.text: Supply athletes with darker headgear

indicators.note: supply read as supple, bendy, so the letters are flexed into a new order

explanation.surface: Provide sportsmen with a darker style of cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like provide, but read it as the adverb of supple.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth cap with front and back peaks, worn by Sherlock Holmes, is a type of hat.

clue.text: OUP person redeployed intentionally

indicators.note: redeployed means put to a new use or position, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker at Oxford University Press is moved to another job deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: OUP is Oxford University Press, but here the letters are only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something deliberately, not by accident, is doing it with a set aim in mind.

clue.text: Butchery involves good stuff

indicators.note: involves means contains, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: gore is the blood of slaughter, butchery

explanation.surface: Slaughter includes some fine material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' looks like a noun meaning material; it is the verb, to stuff oneself with food.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff yourself is to eat greedily until full, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: A deal of trouble from the East draws closer

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means read right to left, backwards

parts.note: to raise a stink is to cause a great deal of trouble

explanation.surface: Trouble arriving from the East brings things closer.
explanation.definitionFit: One knits the brows by drawing them together, and broken bones knit by joining closer.

clue.text: Musician's temper aroused after start-up at intervals

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled temper behind the letters picked from start-up
at intervals means taking every other letter of start-up, the second, fourth and sixth
aroused means stirred up, so the letters of temper are mixed

explanation.surface: A performer's bad mood flares after a shaky beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at intervals' takes TRU from start-up; 'aroused' makes MPETER from TEMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the brass instrument with valves and a bell is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Just clergyman's last pointer disheartened laity

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word clergyman

parts.note: an arrow is a sign that points the way

indicators.note: disheartened means with the heart removed, leaving only the outer letters of laity

explanation.surface: A clergyman's latest guidance dismays the lay members of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Just, as in only barely, matches by a small margin, as in a race won by a whisker.

clue.text: Imprison select group of MPs without support, of course

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the second piece is taken out of the first

parts.note: a select committee is a group of MPs examining an area of policy
on a golf course a tee supports the ball before a drive

explanation.surface: A parliamentary committee lacking backing naturally decides to lock someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but points to the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: To commit someone to prison or a hospital is to send them there and hold them.

clue.text: Manager's journal is here at the centre

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or journal speaking for a group

indicators.note: at the centre takes the middle letters of the word here

explanation.surface: The boss's newspaper is based here at headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arranges and runs things is a coordinator or administrator.

clue.text: Visa mix-up for Spooner? Here's an alternative

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first letters change places

parts.note: a Visa is a credit card
a hash is a muddle or mix-up

explanation.surface: Muddle over a visa means paying another way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here's' is a link: this is offered instead of card payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying in notes and coins is the other option to a credit card such as Visa.

clue.text: Legendary sailor ran off to the borders

indicators.note: the escape is sent to the edges, so it surrounds the sailor

parts.note: fled means ran off
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman escaped to the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something celebrated in story and legend is famed and storied, the stuff of myths.

clue.text: Journalists during stay finding place for an evening tuck-in?

indicators.note: during means within, so the journalists go inside the word for stay

parts.note: to bide is to stay or wait
eds are editors, journalists

explanation.surface: Reporters on a visit look for somewhere for a late supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck-in' looks like a meal; it is being tucked into bed at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Tucking a child in happens at night beside the bed, so it is where that takes place.

clue.text: Exhibit nothing, admitting a digital flaw

parts.note: to hang a picture is to exhibit it

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so a goes inside the word for nothing

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A gallery shows nothing and confesses to a technical fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' suggests computers; here it means to do with the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A torn strip of skin beside a fingernail is a small defect of the finger, a digit.

clue.text: King James's commission in debt, making a statement

parts.note: AV, the Authorised Version of the Bible, was commissioned by King James I
owing means in debt

explanation.surface: A royal order leaves the king in debt, and he makes a declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to declare openly, so avowing is declaring or affirming.

clue.text: Tried and went through in the past

parts.note: had, as in had a bad time, means went through
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Someone attempted and endured things long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Making an attempt at something is an idiomatic way of saying attempted.

clue.text: Above-stairs servant's privy constructed, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals a word heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: the ladies, a women's toilet or privy, was made, that is constructed

explanation.surface: A household servant's lavatory has been built.
explanation.walkthrough: In a grand house 'above stairs' staff waited on the family directly; the ladies is British for a women's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal attendant to the mistress of a house worked with the family, not in the kitchens below.

clue.text: Gradually escape, spanning wide range

indicators.note: spanning means stretching across, so the word for leak goes round the letter for wide

parts.note: to seep is to escape gradually, as liquid
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: Something slowly leaks out across a broad area.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweep of something is its extent or scope, the reach it covers.

clue.text: Halter quickly flipped over mare's back

indicators.note: flipped over means turned the other way, so the word for quickly is read backwards

parts.note: soon means quickly, before long

indicators.note: back points to the final letter of mare

explanation.surface: A horse's head-rope swiftly flicked over the mare's rump.
explanation.definitionFit: A halter can also be a rope with a running loop, as used by a hangman.

clue.text: Cream with fewer calories on last of trifle

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the light version follows the letter from trifle
last of points to the final letter of the word trifle

parts.note: lite is the food-label spelling for a version with fewer calories

explanation.surface: A dessert topping that is lower in calories goes on a trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: Trifle is a British layered pudding of sponge, fruit, custard and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of a group is its best members, the select few at the top.

clue.text: Economist with German husband joining second president

parts.note: John Adams was the second President of the United States
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: An economist and her German spouse meet the second president.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish author of The Wealth of Nations is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth-century Scottish thinker wrote the founding text of classical economics.

clue.text: Be sinless, as US motorists should?

definitions.meaning: to stay on the path of righteousness, avoiding wrong
Americans drive on the right-hand side of the road

explanation.surface: Staying good is like driving correctly in America.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense means staying on the moral path; the other is the rule of the road in America.
